sanskrit: śrotavyaṃ tasya ca raho rakṣyaś cāmātyato bhavet amātyā hy upahantāraṃ bhūyiṣṭhaṃ ghnanti bhārata
english: He must be heard in private, and he must be guarded from the ministers; for the ministers, O Bhārata, most often slay the man who would expose them.

sanskrit: rājakośasya goptāraṃ rājakośavilopakāḥ sametya sarve bādhante sa vinaśyaty arakṣitaḥ
english: The plunderers of the royal treasury band together and harass the guardian of that treasury; left unprotected, he perishes.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam muniḥ kālakavṛkṣīyaḥ kausalyaṃ yad uvāca ha
english: On this point men recount an ancient tale: what the sage Kālakavṛkṣīya once said to the king of Kosala.

sanskrit: kosalānām ādhipatyaṃ saṃprāpte kṣemadarśini muniḥ kālakavṛkṣīya ājagāmeti naḥ śrutam
english: When Kṣemadarśin had attained the sovereignty over the Kosalas, the sage Kālakavṛkṣīya came to him — so we have heard.

sanskrit: sa kākaṃ pañjare baddhvā viṣayaṃ kṣemadarśinaḥ pūrvaṃ paryacarad yuktaḥ pravṛttyarthī punaḥ punaḥ
english: Having confined a crow in a cage, he first went diligently about the realm of Kṣemadarśin, again and again, seeking out intelligence.

sanskrit: adhīye vāyasīṃ vidyāṃ śaṃsanti mama vāyasāḥ anāgatam atītaṃ ca yac ca saṃprati vartate
english: "I have mastered the lore of crows; the crows declare to me what is to come, what is past, and what is happening now."

sanskrit: iti rāṣṭre paripatan bahuśaḥ puruṣaiḥ saha sarveṣāṃ rājayuktānāṃ duṣkṛtaṃ paripṛṣṭavān
english: Roaming thus through the kingdom in the company of many men, he inquired into the misdeeds of all the king's officers.

sanskrit: sa buddhvā tasya rāṣṭrasya vyavasāyaṃ hi sarvaśaḥ rājayuktāpacārāṃś ca sarvān buddhvā tatas tataḥ
english: And when he had learned the whole working of that kingdom in every part, and had learned, here and there, all the offences of the king's officers,

sanskrit: tam eva kākam ādāya rājānaṃ draṣṭum āgamat sarvajño 'smīti vacanaṃ bruvāṇaḥ saṃśitavrataḥ
english: Then, taking that very crow, the sage of stern vows came to see the king, proclaiming, "I am all-knowing."

sanskrit: sa sma kausalyam āgamya rājāmātyam alaṃkṛtam prāha kākasya vacanād amutredaṃ tvayā kṛtam
english: Coming to the king of Kosala, he would say to the adorned royal minister, "By the word of the crow, this deed of yours was done in such-and-such a place;

sanskrit: asau cāsau ca jānīte rājakośas tvayā hṛtaḥ evam ākhyāti kāko 'yaṃ tac chīghram anugamyatām
english: "This man and that man know that the royal treasury was robbed by you. So this crow declares; let it be swiftly looked into."

sanskrit: tathānyān api sa prāha rājakośaharān sadā na cāsya vacanaṃ kiṃ cid akṛtaṃ śrūyate kva cit
english: And so too he denounced the others who were always pilfering the royal treasury; nor was any word of his ever found anywhere to be untrue.

sanskrit: tena viprakṛtāḥ sarve rājayuktāḥ kurūdvaha tam atikramya suptasya niśi kākam apothayan
english: Thus thwarted, all the king's officers, O foremost of the Kurus, went past him by night while he slept and crushed the crow.

sanskrit: vāyasaṃ tu vinirbhinnaṃ dṛṣṭvā bāṇena pañjare pūrvāhṇe brāhmaṇo vākyaṃ kṣemadarśinam abravīt
english: But seeing the crow in the cage pierced through with an arrow, in the forenoon the brāhmaṇa spoke these words to Kṣemadarśin:

sanskrit: rājaṃs tvām abhayaṃ yāce prabhuṃ prāṇadhaneśvaram anujñātas tvayā brūyāṃ vacanaṃ tvatpuro hitam
english: "O king, I beg of you safety — you, the lord and master of my life and wealth; with your leave I would speak words for your good, set before you.

sanskrit: mitrārtham abhisaṃtapto bhaktyā sarvātmanā gataḥ ayaṃ tavārthaṃ harate yo brūyād akṣamānvitaḥ
english: "He who, sore distressed for a friend's sake and gone to him with whole-hearted devotion, should say in vexation, 'This man is robbing your wealth' —

sanskrit: saṃbubodhayiṣur mitraṃ sadaśvam iva sārathiḥ atimanyuprasakto hi prasajya hitakāraṇam
english: "Wishing to rouse his friend to awareness, as a charioteer rouses a good horse, even if, in his earnestness for the other's good, he grows over-zealous —

sanskrit: tathāvidhasya suhṛdaḥ kṣantavyaṃ saṃvijānatā aiśvaryam icchatā nityaṃ puruṣeṇa bubhūṣatā
english: "In such a friend his fault must be forgiven by the discerning man who would prosper, who desires lasting sovereignty."

sanskrit: taṃ rājā pratyuvācedaṃ yan mā kiṃ cid bhavān vadet kasmād ahaṃ na kṣameyam ākāṅkṣann ātmano hitam
english: The king answered him thus: "Whatever you may say to me, why should I not forgive it, seeking as I do my own good?

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa pratijānīhi prabrūhi yadi cecchasi kariṣyāmi hi te vākyaṃ yad yan māṃ vipra vakṣyasi
english: "O brāhmaṇa, give me your assurance, and speak out if you wish; for I shall do whatever you tell me, O sage."

sanskrit: munir uvāca jñātvā nayān apāyāṃś ca bhṛtyatas te bhayāni ca bhaktyā vṛttiṃ samākhyātuṃ bhavato 'ntikam āgamam
english: The sage said: Having learned the courses of policy, the dangers, and the perils that come from your servants, out of devotion I have come into your presence to set forth a rule of conduct.

sanskrit: prāg evoktaś ca doṣo 'yam ācāryair nṛpasevinām agatīkagatir hy eṣā yā rājñā saha jīvikā
english: This fault of those who serve kings was declared long ago by the teachers: that a livelihood spent at a king's side is the last resort of the man who has no other resort.

sanskrit: āśīviṣaiś ca tasyāhuḥ saṃgataṃ yasya rājabhiḥ bahumitrāś ca rājāno bahvamitrās tathaiva ca
english: They say that he who keeps company with kings keeps company with venomous serpents; for kings have many friends, and just as surely many foes.

sanskrit: tebhyaḥ sarvebhya evāhur bhayaṃ rājopasevinām athaiṣām ekato rājan muhūrtād eva bhīr bhavet
english: From all of these, they say, danger comes to the king's attendants; and from these on the one side, O king, fear may arise in but a moment.

sanskrit: naikāntenāpramādo hi kartuṃ śakyo mahīpatau na tu pramādaḥ kartavyaḥ kathaṃ cid bhūtim icchatā
english: Toward a king one cannot keep watchfulness wholly unbroken; yet by no means must the man who desires prosperity ever be careless.

sanskrit: pramādād dhi skhaled rājā skhalite nāsti jīvitam agniṃ dīptam ivāsīded rājānam upaśikṣitaḥ
english: For through one's carelessness a king may stumble, and once he has stumbled there is no surviving him; the well-schooled man should approach a king as he would a blazing fire.

sanskrit: āśīviṣam iva kruddhaṃ prabhuṃ prāṇadhaneśvaram yatnenopacaren nityaṃ nāham asmīti mānavaḥ
english: As though he were an angry venomous serpent, a man should always wait with care upon his lord, the master of his life and wealth, thinking, "I am as good as nothing."

sanskrit: durvyāhṛtāc chaṅkamāno duṣkṛtād duradhiṣṭhitāt durāsitād durvrajitād iṅgitād aṅgaceṣṭitāt
english: Wary of an ill-spoken word, of a misdeed, of a thing badly managed, of sitting wrongly, of walking wrongly, of a gesture, of a movement of the limbs —

sanskrit: devateva hi sarvārthān kuryād rājā prasāditaḥ vaiśvānara iva kruddhaḥ samūlam api nirdahet iti rājan mayaḥ prāha vartate ca tathaiva tat
english: For a king, when pleased, like a god grants every object of desire; but enraged, like the all-consuming fire, he may burn one up root and all. Thus, O king, did Maya declare, and so indeed it stands.

sanskrit: atha bhūyāṃsam evārthaṃ kariṣyāmi punaḥ punaḥ dadāty asmadvidho 'mātyo buddhisāhāyyam āpadi
english: Now I shall make the matter still plainer, again and again: a counsellor such as I lends the aid of his wisdom in time of peril.

sanskrit: vāyasaś caiva me rājann antakāyābhisaṃhitaḥ na ca me 'tra bhavān garhyo na ca yeṣāṃ bhavān priyaḥ hitāhitāṃs tu budhyethā mā parokṣamatir bhava
english: My crow too, O king, was marked out for death; in this I do not blame you, nor those to whom you are dear. But discern who wish you well and who do not; do not let your judgement be a thing kept in the dark.

sanskrit: ye tv ādānaparā eva vasanti bhavato gṛhe abhūtikāmā bhūtānāṃ tādṛśair me 'bhisaṃhitam
english: As for those who dwell in your house bent only on grasping, who wish no welfare to living beings — it was by such as these that my crow was struck down.

sanskrit: ye vā bhavadvināśena rājyam icchanty anantaram antarair abhisaṃdhāya rājan sidhyanti nānyathā
english: Or those who, plotting through hidden agents, desire the kingdom for themselves the moment you are destroyed — they succeed, O king, in no other way than this.

sanskrit: teṣām ahaṃ bhayād rājan gamiṣyāmy anyam āśramam tair hi me saṃdhito bāṇaḥ kāke nipatitaḥ prabho
english: For fear of them, O king, I shall depart to another hermitage; for it was they who aimed the arrow that fell upon the crow, O lord.

sanskrit: chadmanā mama kākaś ca gamito yamasādanam dṛṣṭaṃ hy etan mayā rājaṃs tapodīrgheṇa cakṣuṣā
english: By a stealthy stroke my crow was sent to the abode of Yama; for this I have seen, O king, with the far-seeing eye that austerity has given me.

sanskrit: bahunakrajhaṣagrāhāṃ timiṃgilagaṇāyutām kākena baḍiśenemām atārṣaṃ tvām ahaṃ nadīm
english: Teeming with crocodiles and fish and water-monsters, thronged with shoals of timiṅgilas — that river which is yourself I have crossed, using the crow for a hook.

sanskrit: sthāṇvaśmakaṇṭakavatīṃ vyāghrasiṃhagajākulām durāsadāṃ duṣpraveśāṃ guhāṃ haimavatīm iva
english: Beset with stumps and stones and thorns, swarming with tigers and lions and elephants, hard to approach, hard to enter, like a Himālayan cavern —

sanskrit: agninā tāmasaṃ durgaṃ naubhir āpyaṃ ca gamyate rājadurgāvataraṇe nopāyaṃ paṇḍitā viduḥ
english: A fastness of darkness is passed by fire, a watery one by boats; but for crossing the stronghold that is a king, the learned know no sure means.

sanskrit: gahanaṃ bhavato rājyam andhakāratamovṛtam neha viśvasituṃ śakyaṃ bhavatāpi kuto mayā
english: Your kingdom is an impenetrable thicket, wrapped in murk and gloom; here trust is impossible even for you — how much less for me?

sanskrit: ato nāyaṃ śubho vāsas tulye sadasatī iha vadho hy evātra sukṛte duṣkṛte na ca saṃśayaḥ
english: Therefore no dwelling here is auspicious, where good and evil are reckoned alike; for here, doubtless, death falls upon the well-doer and the ill-doer the same.

sanskrit: nyāyato duṣkṛte ghātaḥ sukṛte syāt kathaṃ vadhaḥ neha yuktaṃ ciraṃ sthātuṃ javenāto vrajed budhaḥ
english: By justice destruction falls upon the evildoer; but how should death come to the well-doer? It is not fitting to stay here long; the wise man should hasten away from here at once.

sanskrit: sītā nāma nadī rājan plavo yasyāṃ nimajjati tathopamām imāṃ manye vāgurāṃ sarvaghātinīm
english: There is a river called Sītā, O king, in which the very raft sinks; like to that, I deem, is this all-destroying snare.

sanskrit: madhuprapāto hi bhavān bhojanaṃ viṣasaṃyutam asatām iva te bhāvo vartate na satām iva āśīviṣaiḥ parivṛtaḥ kūpas tvam iva pārthiva
english: You are like a downpour of honey, like food laced with poison; your disposition runs as the wicked's does, not the good's; you are like a well, O king, ringed about with venomous serpents.

sanskrit: durgatīrthā bṛhatkūlā karīrīvetrasaṃyutā nadī madhurapānīyā yathā rājaṃs tathā bhavān śvagṛdhragomāyuyuto rājahaṃsasamo hy asi
english: As a river of sweet water, but with treacherous fords and high banks, hedged with karīra and cane — even so, O king, are you; and though haunted by dogs and vultures and jackals, you are yet the equal of a royal swan.

sanskrit: yathāśritya mahāvṛkṣaṃ kakṣaḥ saṃvardhate mahān tatas taṃ saṃvṛṇoty eva tam atītya ca vardhate
english: As, taking root beside a great tree, the dense brushwood grows mighty, and then closes over it and, overtopping it, grows on —

sanskrit: tenaivopendhano nūnaṃ dāvo dahati dāruṇaḥ tathopamā hy amātyās te rājaṃs tān pariśodhaya
english: And fed by that very fuel, the dreadful forest-fire surely burns — like to this are your ministers, O king; purge them away.

sanskrit: bhavataiva kṛtā rājan bhavatā paripālitāḥ bhavantaṃ paryavajñāya jighāṃsanti bhavatpriyam
english: Made by you yourself, O king, and cherished by you, they hold you in contempt and seek to slay the one who is dear to you.

sanskrit: uṣitaṃ śaṅkamānena pramādaṃ parirakṣatā antaḥsarpa ivāgāre vīrapatnyā ivālaye śīlaṃ jijñāsamānena rājñaś ca sahajīvinā
english: I have dwelt here suspicious, on my guard against carelessness — like a serpent within the house, like a hero's wife in his hall — wishing to test the character of the king while living at his side.

sanskrit: kaccij jitendriyo rājā kaccid abhyantarā jitāḥ kaccid eṣāṃ priyo rājā kaccid rājñaḥ priyāḥ prajāḥ
english: Has the king mastered his senses? Are his intimates won over? Is the king dear to them? Are the subjects dear to the king?

sanskrit: jijñāsur iha saṃprāptas tavāhaṃ rājasattama tasya me rocase rājan kṣudhitasyeva bhojanam
english: Wishing to learn these things I have come here to you, O best of kings; and you please me, O king, as food pleases a hungry man.

sanskrit: amātyā me na rocante vitṛṣṇasya yathodakam bhavato 'rthakṛd ity eva mayi doṣo hi taiḥ kṛtaḥ vidyate kāraṇaṃ nānyad iti me nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: But your ministers please me not, as water pleases not one whose thirst is quenched; for the very reason that I serve your interest, they have laid a fault upon me — no other cause exists, of this I have no doubt.

sanskrit: na hi teṣām ahaṃ drugdhas tat teṣāṃ doṣavad gatam arer hi durhatād bheyaṃ bhagnapṛṣṭhād ivoragāt
english: For I have done them no injury; that has turned into a grievance with them. One should fear an enemy ill-struck, as one fears a serpent with its back but broken.

sanskrit: rājovāca bhūyasā paribarheṇa satkāreṇa ca bhūyasā pūjito brāhmaṇaśreṣṭha bhūyo vasa gṛhe mama
english: The king said: With greater retinue and greater honour, held in greater esteem, O best of brāhmaṇas, dwell yet again in my house.

sanskrit: ye tvāṃ brāhmaṇa necchanti na te vatsyanti me gṛhe bhavataiva hi taj jñeyaṃ yad idānīm anantaram
english: Those who do not want you, O brāhmaṇa, shall not dwell in my house; and you yourself shall determine what is now to be done forthwith.

sanskrit: yathā syād duṣkṛto daṇḍo yathā ca sukṛtaṃ kṛtam tathā samīkṣya bhagavañ śreyase viniyuṅkṣva mām
english: How the evildoer should be punished, and how the good deed should be rewarded — having considered these, O reverend one, appoint me to whatever is best.

sanskrit: munir uvāca adarśayann imaṃ doṣam ekaikaṃ durbalaṃ kuru tataḥ kāraṇam ājñāya puruṣaṃ puruṣaṃ jahi
english: The sage said: Without revealing this design, weaken them one by one; then, having found out the cause, do away with each man in turn.

sanskrit: ekadoṣā hi bahavo mṛdnīyur api kaṇṭakān mantrabhedabhayād rājaṃs tasmād etad bravīmi te
english: For many men, banded together by a common grievance, may crush even thorns; from fear that your counsel be betrayed, O king, I tell you this.

sanskrit: vayaṃ tu brāhmaṇā nāma mṛdudaṇḍāḥ kṛpālavaḥ svasti cecchāmi bhavataḥ pareṣāṃ ca yathātmanaḥ
english: But we who are called brāhmaṇas are mild in punishment and full of compassion; and I wish well to you, and to others, as to my own self.

sanskrit: rājann ātmānam ācakṣe saṃbandhī bhavato hy aham muniḥ kālakavṛkṣīya ity evam abhisaṃjñitaḥ
english: O king, I declare myself to you — for I am a kinsman of yours; I am the sage known by the name Kālakavṛkṣīya.

sanskrit: pituḥ sakhā ca bhavataḥ saṃmataḥ satyasaṃgaraḥ vyāpanne bhavato rājye rājan pitari saṃsthite
english: I was your father's friend, esteemed by him, true to my word. When your kingdom had fallen into ruin, O king, and your father had passed away,

sanskrit: sarvakāmān parityajya tapas taptaṃ tadā mayā snehāt tvāṃ prabravīmy etan mā bhūyo vibhramed iti
english: Renouncing every desire, I then practised austerity. Out of affection I tell you this, that you may not go astray again.

sanskrit: ubhe dṛṣṭvā duḥkhasukhe rājyaṃ prāpya yadṛcchayā rājyenāmātyasaṃsthena kathaṃ rājan pramādyasi
english: Having seen both sorrow and joy, and having won a kingdom by good fortune, how, O king, can you be heedless of a realm that rests in the hands of its ministers?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato rājakule nāndī saṃjajñe bhūyasī punaḥ purohitakule caiva saṃprāpte brāhmaṇarṣabhe
english: Bhīṣma said: Thereupon, when that bull among brāhmaṇas had been received into the house of the royal chaplain, great rejoicing once more arose in the royal family.

sanskrit: ekacchatrāṃ mahīṃ kṛtvā kausalyāya yaśasvine muniḥ kālakavṛkṣīya īje kratubhir uttamaiḥ
english: Having made the earth subject to a single parasol for the renowned king of Kosala, the sage Kālakavṛkṣīya performed sacrifices with the highest rites.

sanskrit: hitaṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā kausalyo 'nvaśiṣan mahīm tathā ca kṛtavān rājā yathoktaṃ tena bhārata
english: Having heard that salutary counsel, the king of Kosala ruled the earth; and the king did, O Bhārata, even as the sage had told him.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca hrīniṣedhāḥ sadā santaḥ satyārjavasamanvitāḥ śaktāḥ kathayituṃ samyak te tava syuḥ sabhāsadaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Men ever good, restrained by modesty, endowed with truth and rectitude, able to speak rightly — let such be your members of council.

sanskrit: atyāḍhyāṃś cātiśūrāṃś ca brāhmaṇāṃś ca bahuśrutān susaṃtuṣṭāṃś ca kaunteya mahotsāhāṃś ca karmasu
english: Men of great wealth and great valour, and brāhmaṇas of wide learning, well contented, O son of Kuntī, and of great energy in their tasks —

sanskrit: etān sahāyāṃl lipsethāḥ sarvāsv āpatsu bhārata kulīnaḥ pūjito nityaṃ na hi śaktiṃ nigūhati
english: Seek such men as helpers in all calamities, O Bhārata; for a man of good family, ever honoured, does not conceal his strength.

sanskrit: prasannaṃ hy aprasannaṃ vā pīḍitaṃ hṛtam eva vā āvartayati bhūyiṣṭhaṃ tad eko hy anupālitaḥ
english: For whether pleased or displeased, whether oppressed or despoiled, he most often turns the matter back to good — when such a one, even single, is cherished.

sanskrit: kulīnā deśajāḥ prājñā rūpavanto bahuśrutāḥ pragalbhāś cānuraktāś ca te tava syuḥ paricchadāḥ
english: Men of good birth, native to the land, wise, comely, of wide learning, bold and devoted — let such be your retinue.

sanskrit: dauṣkuleyāś ca lubdhāś ca nṛśaṃsā nirapatrapāḥ te tvāṃ tāta niṣeveyur yāvad ārdrakapāṇayaḥ
english: But the base-born, the greedy, the cruel, the shameless — these, my son, will wait upon you only so long as their palms are still moist.

sanskrit: arthamānārghyasatkārair bhogair uccāvacaiḥ priyān yān arthabhājo manyethās te te syuḥ sukhabhāginaḥ
english: With wealth and honour and homage and esteem, and with enjoyments high and low, whomever among your favourites you judge deserving of substance — let them have their share of comfort.

sanskrit: abhinnavṛttā vidvāṃsaḥ sadvṛttāś caritavratāḥ na tvāṃ nityārthino jahyur akṣudrāḥ satyavādinaḥ
english: The learned of unbroken conduct, of good ways, who have kept their vows — such men, never mean and ever truthful, will not forsake you, though they look constantly to your bounty.

sanskrit: anāryā ye na jānanti samayaṃ mandacetasaḥ tebhyaḥ pratijugupsethā jānīyāḥ samayacyutān
english: The ignoble, dull of mind, who do not know what is fitting — guard yourself against these, and mark out those who have fallen from their covenants.

sanskrit: naikam icched gaṇaṃ hitvā syāc ced anyataragrahaḥ yas tv eko bahubhiḥ śreyān kāmaṃ tena gaṇaṃ tyajet
english: One should not, forsaking a whole body of men, set one's heart on a single man, were a choice to be made between them; but if one man be better than many, then by all means let him give up the many for that one.

sanskrit: śreyaso lakṣaṇaṃ hy etad vikramo yasya dṛśyate kīrtipradhāno yaś ca syāt samaye yaś ca tiṣṭhati
english: For this is the mark of a superior man: in whom valour is seen, who holds renown foremost, and who stands fast by his covenant.

sanskrit: samarthān pūjayed yaś ca nāspardhyaiḥ spardhate ca yaḥ na ca kāmād bhayāt krodhāl lobhād vā dharmam utsṛjet
english: Who honours the capable, who does not contend with those past contending, and who, from desire, fear, anger, or greed, never casts off dharma —

sanskrit: amānī satyavāk śakto jitātmā mānyamānitā sa te mantrasahāyaḥ syāt sarvāvasthaṃ parīkṣitaḥ
english: Free of pride, truthful, capable, master of himself, honouring those worthy of honour — such a man, tested in every condition, may be your companion in counsel.

sanskrit: kulīnaḥ satyasaṃpannas titikṣur dakṣa ātmavān śūraḥ kṛtajñaḥ satyaś ca śreyasaḥ pārtha lakṣaṇam
english: Well-born, possessed of truth, enduring, capable, self-possessed, brave, grateful, and honest — this, O Pārtha, is the mark of a superior man.

sanskrit: tasyaivaṃ vartamānasya puruṣasya vijānataḥ amitrāḥ saṃprasīdanti tato mitrībhavanty api
english: When such a man, discerning, conducts himself in this way, even his enemies grow well-disposed and thereafter become his friends.
